inputs.name: dE
inputs.constraints: Finite scalar; RK4 requires Poisson consistency within rtol=1e-12,atol=1e-14.

inputs.name: vv
inputs.constraints: Finite one-dimensional; aligned with df and df0dv when applicable.

inputs.name: df0dv
inputs.description: Equilibrium derivative or declared forcing on velocity nodes.
inputs.constraints: Finite one-dimensional aligned vector; can include quadrature-deposited jump masses.

inputs.name: dt
inputs.description: Time step in inverse plasma frequency.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: The updated distribution and its Poisson-closed field are returned positionally as the tuple (new_df, new_dE). Unpack the tuple in that order; inputs are not modified.
outputs.constraints: Finite updated distribution and field preserving discrete Poisson closure.

preconditions: df, vv and df0dv are finite aligned one-dimensional vectors.
dE satisfies discrete Poisson closure; k and dv are finite with k nonzero and dv positive; dt is positive.
supported: One classical RK4 step with Poisson closure recomputed at every stage.
excluded: Nonlinear evolution, multidimensional modes and unconstrained incoming fields.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError for invalid arrays/scalars or an incoming dE outside the declared Poisson tolerance.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: FloatingPointError when an intermediate or updated state/field is nonfinite.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; exactly one prescribed step is evaluated.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No updated tuple is returned after an exception.

python.signature: vp_rk4_step(df, dE, vv, df0dv, k, dv, dt)

example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.kinetic import vp_init, vp_rk4_step
s = vp_init(nv=32)
step = vp_rk4_step(*(s[n] for n in ('df', 'dE', 'vv', 'df0dv', 'k', 'dv', 'dt')))
assert isinstance(step, tuple)
f, E = step
assert f.shape == (33,) and np.iscomplexobj(f)
assert np.isscalar(E) and np.iscomplexobj(E)
example.description: Advance one Poisson-closed RK4 step from a 32-interval initial state.
example.expected: The tuple unpacks into a complex distribution of shape (33,) followed by a complex scalar field.

scope: Independent reference: two sources that do not read the implementation's stages. The classical four-stage tableau is re-derived at 40 digits together with the discrete mass identity d(rho)/dt = -i k j + E (dv sum f0'), and the semidiscrete initial-value problem is solved by scipy.linalg.expm, an independent Padé algorithm; the order is the measured refinement ratio, not a quoted constant.

Implementation relation: the four stages use the Poisson closure vp_field(state) internally, so the field is re-closed at every stage instead of being advanced as an independent variable; the incoming dE must satisfy the closure within rtol = 1e-12, atol = 1e-14 and is rejected otherwise; the returned field is the closure of the returned state.

Test matrix: the fourth-order ratio on the built-in 2049-node configuration, the discrete mass identity with a wrong final weight as the discriminating control, the closure of the returned field, the unclosed-incoming-field rejection, and a non-representable state that must raise FloatingPointError rather than return NaN.

Precision budget, declared before the comparison was run: the measured refinement ratio must lie in [14, 18] for a predicted 16 (roundoff window measured on this configuration, printed by the assertion), and the mass identity uses 64 eps of the largest stage term because the quadrature is a cancelled sum.

Evidence ceiling: fourth order is declared only for the configuration actually measured; the ratio is not a proof of order for grids or step sizes outside it, and no stability boundary is established.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Independent semidiscrete mathematical and selected scenario regressions; actual run/installed-wheel receipts are recorded separately, not inferred from test existence.
known_limitations: Finite-window rectangle rule and sampling recurrence TR=2pi/(k*dv).
Fn4 truncated density retains original coefficient and is not renormalized after cutoff.
Peak diagnostic assumes standing oscillation; rotating complex exponential has no amplitude peaks.
